sbom_standards.description: Identifies the document as a CycloneDX BOM. This is the primary discriminator for parsers to determine the format of the document. It must always be set to 'CycloneDX'. This field, combined with specVersion, enables tools to correctly parse and validate the SBOM against the appropriate specification version.
sbom_standards.validation_rules: Must be exactly 'CycloneDX'. Case-sensitive. Required in JSON format; in XML, the namespace serves this purpose.
sbom_standards.equivalent_field: SPDXVersion (SPDX, serves a similar format identification purpose)

sbom_standards.description: Specifies the CycloneDX specification version the BOM conforms to. This determines which fields are valid, which enumerations are available, and how the document should be validated. CycloneDX 1.6 introduced significant new features including attestations, cryptographic bill of materials (CBOM), and enhanced environmental impact tracking.
sbom_standards.validation_rules: Must be a valid CycloneDX specification version string. For CycloneDX 1.6, the value must be '1.6'.

sbom_standards.description: A unique identifier for this specific BOM instance. The serial number, combined with the version field, provides a globally unique identifier for a specific revision of the BOM. This is essential for BOM lifecycle management, allowing consumers to determine if they have the latest version and to track BOM updates over time.
sbom_standards.validation_rules: Should be a valid URN using UUID format: 'urn:uuid:' followed by a valid UUID v4. While not strictly required, it is strongly recommended for production SBOMs.

sbom_standards.description: The version of this BOM document. When a BOM is updated (e.g., after a rebuild with different dependencies), the version should be incremented while the serialNumber remains the same. This enables consumers to track the evolution of a specific BOM over time and ensure they are using the most current revision.
sbom_standards.validation_rules: Must be a positive integer. Starts at 1 for the initial version. Must be incremented for each update to the same BOM (same serialNumber).
sbom_standards.equivalent_field: No direct equivalent (SPDX uses DocumentNamespace versioning)

sbom_standards.description: The date and time when the BOM was created. This timestamp is critical for determining the freshness of the SBOM and establishing when the inventory was accurate. In regulated environments like EU CRA compliance, maintaining temporal accuracy of SBOMs is a requirement for demonstrating ongoing security monitoring.
sbom_standards.validation_rules: Must be in ISO 8601 format. UTC timezone recommended. Example: '2024-06-15T14:30:00Z'.

sbom_standards.description: Describes the tools used to create the BOM, including SBOM generators, scanners, and analysis tools. In CycloneDX 1.6, tools can be described either as a legacy array of tool objects or as 'components' and 'services' for richer metadata. Tool identification enables consumers to assess BOM quality based on known tool capabilities and limitations.
sbom_standards.validation_rules: In CycloneDX 1.6, the preferred format is metadata.tools.components[] (array of component objects). Legacy format metadata.tools[] (array of tool objects with vendor, name, version) is deprecated but supported.

sbom_standards.description: Describes the primary component that the BOM represents. This is the software application or library for which the SBOM is being generated. It establishes the subject of the BOM, distinguishing it from the components listed in the components[] array which are its dependencies. The metadata.component is analogous to the 'root' of the dependency tree.
sbom_standards.validation_rules: Must be a valid component object with at minimum 'type' and 'name' fields. Should include 'version' and 'purl' for full identification.

sbom_standards.description: Classifies the type of component. CycloneDX 1.6 supports a comprehensive set of component types including application, framework, library, container, platform, device, firmware, file, machine-learning-model, data, device-driver, and cryptographic-asset. Accurate typing enables downstream tooling to apply type-specific policies and analysis.
sbom_standards.validation_rules: Must be one of the enumerated values: application, framework, library, container, platform, device, firmware, file, machine-learning-model, data, device-driver, cryptographic-asset. Most common for software SBOMs: library, framework, application.
sbom_standards.equivalent_field: No direct equivalent (SPDX uses PackagePurpose which has different values)

sbom_standards.description: The name of the component. This should be the canonical name as used by the component's ecosystem. For npm packages, this includes the scope prefix (e.g., @angular/core). For Maven artifacts, this is the artifactId. Consistent naming is critical for accurate vulnerability correlation and dependency resolution across tools.
sbom_standards.validation_rules: Non-empty string. Should match the canonical name from the component's native package registry or repository.

sbom_standards.description: The version string of the component. While not strictly required by the schema, omitting version information dramatically reduces SBOM utility since vulnerability databases, license databases, and dependency resolution all depend on precise version identification. Strongly recommended for all components.
sbom_standards.validation_rules: Should follow the versioning convention of the component's ecosystem (semver for npm, Maven versioning for Java, etc.). No specific format enforced by the schema.

sbom_standards.description: Package URL (purl) is a standardized format for uniquely identifying software packages across ecosystems. It is the most important field for interoperability and vulnerability correlation. Purls enable tools to match components against vulnerability databases (OSV, NVD), license databases, and other security data sources without ecosystem-specific logic.
sbom_standards.validation_rules: Must conform to the Package URL specification (https://github.com/package-url/purl-spec). Format: 'pkg:TYPE/NAMESPACE/NAME@VERSION?QUALIFIERS#SUBPATH'. Type is required (npm, maven, pypi, golang, etc.).

sbom_standards.description: A unique reference identifier for a component within the BOM. This identifier is used in the dependencies[] array to express dependency relationships between components. While optional in the schema, it is effectively required if you want to represent the dependency graph, which is a core value proposition of SBOMs.
sbom_standards.validation_rules: Must be unique within the BOM. Any string value is acceptable. Common convention is to use the purl or a UUID. Referenced by dependencies[].ref and dependencies[].dependsOn[].

sbom_standards.description: Cryptographic hash values of the component's distribution artifact. Multiple hash algorithms can be specified for the same component. Hashes enable integrity verification, ensuring that the actual component used matches what was declared in the SBOM. This is a critical supply chain security control against tampering.
sbom_standards.validation_rules: Array of objects with 'alg' (algorithm) and 'content' (hash value) fields. Supported algorithms: MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384, SHA-512, SHA3-256, SHA3-384, SHA3-512, BLAKE2b-256, BLAKE2b-384, BLAKE2b-512, BLAKE3.

sbom_standards.description: The license(s) associated with the component. Each license can be expressed as an SPDX license ID, an SPDX license expression, or a named license with full license text. Accurate license data is essential for open source compliance programs and is increasingly required by regulations such as the EU Cyber Resilience Act.
sbom_standards.validation_rules: Array of license choice objects. Each can contain either a 'license' object (with 'id' for SPDX ID or 'name' for non-SPDX licenses) or an 'expression' string using SPDX expression syntax.

sbom_standards.description: Identifies the organization that supplied the component. This is distinct from the author/publisher and represents the entity from which the component was obtained. Under the EU Cyber Resilience Act, accurate supplier identification is a regulatory requirement for products with digital elements sold in the European market.
sbom_standards.validation_rules: Object with optional fields: name (string), url (array of URLs), contact (array of contact objects with name, email, phone).

sbom_standards.description: Specifies the scope of the component within the project. This distinguishes between components needed at runtime versus those used only during development or testing. Scope information helps consumers focus vulnerability remediation on components that actually ship in production, reducing noise from dev-only dependencies.
sbom_standards.validation_rules: Must be one of: 'required' (needed at runtime), 'optional' (may be needed at runtime), 'excluded' (not included in the final build). Default if omitted is 'required'.
sbom_standards.equivalent_field: Relationship type (SPDX: DEPENDS_ON vs DEV_DEPENDENCY_OF vs OPTIONAL_DEPENDENCY_OF)

sbom_standards.description: Links to external resources related to the component, such as documentation, issue trackers, VCS repositories, advisories, and distribution sources. External references enrich the SBOM with contextual information that aids in vulnerability triage, incident response, and compliance auditing by providing direct links to relevant resources.
sbom_standards.validation_rules: Array of objects with 'type' (enum) and 'url' (string) fields. Optional 'comment' and 'hashes' fields. Types include: vcs, issue-tracker, website, advisories, bom, mailing-list, social, chat, documentation, support, source-distribution, distribution, distribution-intake, license, build-meta, build-system, release-notes, security-contact, model-card, log, configuration, evidence, formulation, attestation, threat-model, adversary-model, risk-assessment, vulnerability-assertion, exploitability-statement, pentest-report, static-analysis-report, dynamic-analysis-report, runtime-analysis-report, component-analysis-report, maturity-report, certification-report, codified-infrastructure, quality-metrics, poam, electronic-signature, digital-signature.

sbom_standards.description: A list of known vulnerabilities affecting components in the BOM. CycloneDX is unique among SBOM formats in natively supporting Vulnerability Exploitability eXchange (VEX) data within the BOM itself. This enables software producers to communicate vulnerability status (affected, not affected, under investigation, fixed) alongside the component inventory.
sbom_standards.validation_rules: Array of vulnerability objects. Each requires at minimum an 'id' field. Recommended fields: source (database), ratings (severity), description, recommendation, analysis (state, justification, response), affects (list of affected component bom-refs with version ranges).
sbom_standards.equivalent_field: No direct equivalent (SPDX uses separate SPDX Security documents for VEX)

sbom_standards.description: Describes the dependency relationships between components in the BOM. Each entry identifies a component (via bom-ref) and lists the bom-refs of components it directly depends on. This forms a directed acyclic graph representing the dependency tree, which is essential for transitive vulnerability analysis and understanding blast radius.
sbom_standards.validation_rules: Array of objects with 'ref' (the component's bom-ref) and 'dependsOn' (array of bom-refs this component depends on). Every bom-ref used must correspond to a component or service in the BOM.

sbom_standards.description: Describes the completeness of the BOM with respect to its components and dependencies. This is a critical trust signal: a BOM that declares its composition as 'complete' asserts that all components are enumerated, while 'incomplete' or 'unknown' signals that additional components may exist but are not listed. This enables consumers to assess SBOM quality and coverage.
sbom_standards.validation_rules: Array of objects with 'aggregate' (enum: complete, incomplete, incomplete_first_party_only, incomplete_first_party_proprietary_only, incomplete_first_party_openSource_only, incomplete_third_party_only, incomplete_third_party_proprietary_only, incomplete_third_party_openSource_only, unknown, not_specified) and optional 'assemblies' or 'dependencies' (arrays of bom-refs).
sbom_standards.equivalent_field: No direct equivalent (SPDX does not have a compositional completeness assertion)

sbom_standards.description: Identifies the lifecycle phase during which the BOM was generated. CycloneDX 1.6 supports lifecycle phases including design, pre-build, build, post-build, operations, discovery, and decommission. This contextualizes the BOM for consumers, as SBOMs generated at build time vs. runtime analysis will have different completeness characteristics.
sbom_standards.validation_rules: Array of lifecycle objects with 'phase' enum or 'name' and 'description' for custom phases. Standard phases: design, pre-build, build, post-build, operations, discovery, decommission.
sbom_standards.equivalent_field: No direct equivalent (SPDX does not distinguish BOM lifecycle phases)

sbom_standards.description: Describes the build environment and process used to produce the software. Formulation captures CI/CD pipeline details, build tool configurations, environment variables, and other build reproducibility information. This aligns with SLSA provenance requirements and supports build reproducibility verification as part of supply chain security.
sbom_standards.validation_rules: Array of formula objects containing 'components' (build tools), 'services' (build services), 'workflows' (build steps), and 'properties'. Each workflow can contain tasks with steps.
sbom_standards.equivalent_field: No direct equivalent (SPDX 2.3 does not capture build formulation; planned for SPDX 3.0)

sbom_standards.description: Provides evidence of how a component was identified and what its actual usage is within the software. Evidence includes identity evidence (how the component was detected), occurrence evidence (where in the codebase it appears), and callstack evidence (how it is invoked at runtime). This supports SBOM accuracy verification and reduces false positives.
sbom_standards.validation_rules: Object with optional 'identity' (detection method and confidence), 'occurrences' (file locations), and 'callstack' (runtime call evidence) fields. Identity confidence is a decimal between 0 and 1.
sbom_standards.equivalent_field: No direct equivalent (SPDX does not have component-level evidence)

sbom_standards.description: New in CycloneDX 1.6, declarations enable attesting to standards, claims, and evidence about the software. This supports compliance frameworks like EU CRA, SSDF, and SLSA by allowing producers to formally declare conformance and provide supporting evidence within the SBOM itself. Declarations link assessors, attestations, claims, evidence, and targets.
sbom_standards.validation_rules: Object with optional 'assessors', 'attestations', 'claims', 'evidence', 'targets', 'affirmation', and 'signature' fields. Attestations reference assessors and map claims to evidence with compliance mappings.
sbom_standards.equivalent_field: No equivalent (SPDX 2.3 does not support attestations/declarations)

sbom_standards.description: A name-value store for additional metadata that extends the BOM with custom or domain-specific information. Properties can appear at multiple levels: BOM-level, component-level, service-level, and vulnerability-level. CycloneDX defines standardized property namespaces (e.g., cdx:) for common use cases, while organizations can define their own namespaces for custom data.
sbom_standards.validation_rules: Array of objects with 'name' (string) and 'value' (string) fields. Names should use namespace prefixes to avoid collisions (e.g., 'cdx:npm:package:bundled', 'internal:team:security').
sbom_standards.equivalent_field: No direct equivalent (SPDX uses Annotation for some similar purposes)
